problem: Amazon removed the web 'Download & Transfer via USB' option on 26 Feb 2025, so buyers can no longer pull a local backup copy of purchased books from the website. It hit a minority of owners directly, but it made the 'you own a license, not a book' issue visible to everyone.

sources.title: Cloudwards: Amazon removes USB download & transfer
AlternativeTo news: removal by Feb 2025
Libreture: Amazon removing your ability to download and keep ebooks
Rossmann Group wiki entry

workarounds: Send to a Kindle over Wi-Fi, then copy KFX files off by USB; buy from DRM-free stores instead.
saga_solution: Every imported file stays a plain file the user can see in the OS file manager; a one-tap 'Export library' writes originals + annotations + metadata to a folder or zip, with no account needed.

problem: Amazon now lets KDP authors who sell DRM-free let buyers download EPUB/PDF copies (announced Dec 2025, from Jan 2026). Readers welcomed it, but it only covers the titles where the author opted out of DRM, so most of a typical Kindle library is unaffected.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: DRM-free Kindle ebooks downloadable as EPUB/PDF
TechCrunch: Amazon changes how DRM applies to KDP ebooks
The Bookseller: download of some e-books from 2026

workarounds: Check each title's DRM status; download eligible EPUBs manually.
saga_solution: Make SAGA the obvious destination for these newly downloadable DRM-free EPUB/PDFs: share-sheet import from Amazon's download page, dedupe against existing copies, keep the original file untouched.

problem: Independent traffic analysis found the Kindle app reports very fine-grained reading behaviour (page timestamps, character positions, taps, settings changes) and queues it while offline for later upload. Most readers never look, but privacy-minded users cite it as a reason to leave.

sources.title: Nullsweep: Kindle collects a surprisingly large amount of data
Reclaim The Net: On Kindle, Amazon tracks your every tap
Input: Amazon tracks every tap on your Kindle

workarounds: Keep the device in airplane mode; use KOReader or an offline reader.
saga_solution: No reading telemetry by default; reading stats computed and stored on-device; any opt-in crash reporting excludes book titles and positions; publish a plain-language data inventory.

problem: Mozilla's Privacy Not Included rated Onyx Boox 'very creepy': no device-specific privacy policy found, unconfirmed security update practice, and no reply to inquiries. Boox users get great hardware flexibility but little transparency.

sources.title: Mozilla Privacy Not Included: Onyx Boox
MobileRead thread on Boox data/privacy

workarounds: Block vendor apps with a firewall; use third-party reader apps on Boox.
saga_solution: SAGA Leaf firmware ships with a published privacy policy, no cloud dependency, and open update notes; the app works with the Leaf over local transfer only unless the user opts into sync.

problem: Kobo is repeatedly praised because buyers can still download their purchased books and sideload freely, which reviewers frame as more ownership than Kindle allows.

sources.title: Laptop Mag: I switched from Kindle to Kobo for a week
Johnny Jet: why I switched from Kindle Oasis to Kobo Libra Colour

saga_solution: Match Kobo's openness and go further: no store lock-in at all, any DRM-free file is a first-class book.

problem: Kindle devices no longer show covers for books sideloaded over USB or Wi-Fi on some models (titles appear as text tiles), which reviewers call a deliberate or neglected degradation of non-Amazon content.

sources.title: Tom's Guide: Kindle Colorsoft shortcoming with sideloaded covers
Book Riot: How to fix missing covers on sideloaded Kindle ebooks
The eBook Reader: personal documents show covers on lockscreen but not library

workarounds: Calibre 'fix covers' on device; send via Send-to-Kindle instead of USB.
saga_solution: Treat sideloaded books identically to any other: extract the EPUB cover, let the user replace it, and push the same thumbnail to SAGA Leaf.

problem: The Xteink X4 does not mount as a USB drive, so books go on via microSD or a browser upload to the device's local IP. Owners find this fiddly compared with drag-and-drop.

sources.title: PocketInk: Xteink X4 pre-purchase reality check
Digital Trends: Xteink X4 review

workarounds: microSD card reader; CrossPoint firmware Wi-Fi upload or Calibre wireless.
saga_solution: SAGA Leaf: pair once with the phone app (BLE handshake, Wi-Fi/BLE bulk transfer) and push books from the SAGA library with one tap; also expose USB mass storage as a fallback.

problem: Kobo's built-in Instapaper integration (replacing Pocket after Mozilla shut Pocket in July 2025) was received as Kobo 'saving' a favourite feature: read-later articles appear on the e-reader.

sources.title: Kobo Help: Pocket has shut down
Android Authority: Kobo Instapaper integration rolls out
Boing Boing: Kobo just saved one of its e-readers' best features

saga_solution: Let SAGA import web articles (share-sheet, Instapaper/Wallabag/Readwise via OPML or API) and push them to SAGA Leaf as clean reflowable text.

problem: Pocket's shutdown deleted users' saved items after the export window closed (Oct 2025), a reminder that read-later and reading data held by a third party can vanish.

sources.title: Kobo Help: Pocket has shut down
Good e-Reader: Will you buy a Kobo now that Pocket is discontinued?

workarounds: Export to HTML/CSV before the deadline; move to Instapaper.
saga_solution: All saved articles and highlights live locally in an open format (EPUB/Markdown + JSON); if SAGA's cloud ever ends, nothing is lost.

problem: Kobo does not sync reading position or annotations for sideloaded books across devices and apps, and Kindle only syncs personal documents sent via Send-to-Kindle, not USB sideloads. Readers with DRM-free libraries lose the 'pick up anywhere' experience that store buyers get.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: Nook can sync sideloaded ebooks now (compares Kindle/Kobo)
The eBook Reader: sync issues with Kobo finally fixed (purchased only)
MobileRead: Kobo sideloaded sync thread

workarounds: KOReader progress sync server; Calibre-Web/Kobo sync hacks; Send-to-Kindle.
saga_solution: Position + highlight sync keyed by content hash (not filename), working identically for every imported file across phone, desktop, web and SAGA Leaf; end-to-end encrypted.

problem: Kobo's own bookmark/progress sync between e-readers and apps was unreliable long enough that Kobo rebuilt the system in 2026; users must manually run 'Repair account' or re-sign-in on each device to get the fix.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: sync issues with Kobo ereaders and apps finally fixed
Notebookcheck: Kobo finally fixes longstanding issues

workarounds: Manually note page; repair account per device.
saga_solution: Show sync state explicitly (last synced, from which device) and offer 'jump to furthest position' with conflict choice rather than silently overwriting.

problem: Whispersync (position, highlights, notes moving seamlessly across Kindle devices and apps) is one of the features that keeps people on Kindle even when they dislike Amazon.

sources.title: Android Authority: the Kindle feature stopping me switching
SlashGear: 3 things Kindle owners say they love most

saga_solution: Parity is mandatory: sync must 'just work' with zero configuration for users who opt in, including the Leaf.

problem: Open-source readers rely on partial sync: KOReader's official sync server handles progress only, and matching can break if filenames or file contents differ; annotation sync needs third-party plugins (Readest server, Syncthing, AnnotationSync).

sources.title: Readest wiki: Sync with KOReader devices
AnnotationSync.koplugin release
koreader-syncthing plugin

workarounds: Syncthing folder sync of sidecar files; Readest plugin; manual export.
saga_solution: Interoperate: speak the KOReader progress-sync protocol so existing KOReader devices can sync with SAGA, and offer annotation sync natively.

problem: Desktop-only readers such as Foliate have no built-in cross-device progress sync, so users write tutorials for syncing config folders between computers.

sources.title: EndeavourOS forum: how to sync reading progress in Foliate
Foliate (Wikipedia)

saga_solution: Ship a Linux/desktop client with the same sync engine instead of leaving desktop as an afterthought.

problem: Apple's iOS 16 Books redesign hid controls behind a menu, replaced the page-curl with a card-slide animation, and added accidental double-tap bookmarks; enough users objected that Apple restored the curl option in iOS 16.4.

sources.title: Michael Tsai: Apple Books in iOS 16
MacRumors forum: I truly despise the iOS 16 Apple Books update
TidBITS talk: How Apple's Books app changed in iOS 16

saga_solution: Never force a UI redesign on readers: keep page-turn style, chrome visibility and tap zones as user settings that survive updates.

problem: Kobo readers praise the typography control (more built-in fonts, weight/sharpness sliders, easy custom font loading), which is a common reason given for switching from Kindle.

sources.title: Laptop Mag: Kindle vs Kobo hands-on
Avocado Diaries: Why I'm switching from Kindle to Kobo

saga_solution: Ship good defaults plus weight/sharpness, margins, line spacing, hyphenation and drag-in custom fonts on every platform, including the Leaf.

problem: Publisher/author CSS often makes ebooks look bad on Kindle (forced fonts, odd spacing), and readers cannot always override it.

sources.title: BookFunnel blog: why do ebooks look ugly on Kindle

workarounds: Edit the EPUB in Calibre/Sigil; use publisher font toggle.
saga_solution: Provide a 'publisher styles: full / partial / off' switch per book, as KOReader does with style tweaks.

problem: Stock Xteink X4 software forces justified text, offers no margin control, limited fonts and broken bold/italic, and sometimes defaults to Chinese; reviewers say the open CrossPoint firmware is what makes it pleasant.

sources.title: Aftermath: Xteink X4 cheap hackable e-reader / CrossPoint review
Digital Trends: Xteink X4 review

saga_solution: SAGA Leaf must ship with good typography out of the box (margin, alignment, line height, bold/italic, a crisp small-screen font) rather than relying on community firmware.

problem: Reviewers love the card-sized, ~77 g, magnetic phone-back form of the Xteink X4: always with you, cheap (~$69) and comfortable for long sessions with ~2 weeks of battery.

sources.title: Digital Trends: Xteink X4 review
Aftermath: Xteink X4 review
Boing Boing: Xteink X4 MagSafes to your wallet

saga_solution: Validates SAGA Leaf's concept; keep it light, cheap, magnetic and long-lasting.

problem: On a 4.3-inch 220 ppi screen only a few paragraphs fit per page and text is softer than 300 ppi readers; the original X4 also lacks a front light and touch, so reading in bed needs a clip-on lamp.

sources.title: Digital Trends: Xteink X4 review
PocketInk: Xteink X4 reality check
Digital Trends: Xteink X4 Pro review (adds front light)

workarounds: Clip-on light; smallest font; buy X4 Pro.
saga_solution: Leaf: include a front light, a font tuned for small sizes, tight-but-readable default margins, and an optional 'compact' layout that hides headers/footers.

problem: Large camera bumps on newer phones stop magnetic phone-back readers sitting flush, so they rock or overhang.

sources.title: Digital Trends: Xteink X4 review
Aftermath: Xteink X4 review

workarounds: Use on a case or wallet; adhesive ring offset.
saga_solution: Design the Leaf's magnet ring and back geometry around current camera-bump layouts; offer a slim wallet/case variant.

problem: KOReader on PocketBook was faster for PDFs but crashed occasionally on first load of large PDFs, and loading screens interrupt the flow.

sources.title: TechTactician: PocketBook Verse Pro with KOReader after 4 months

workarounds: Pre-open big PDFs on a charger; use stock reader for EPUB.
saga_solution: Index/render big PDFs in the background with progress, cache rendered pages, and recover gracefully from render failures without losing position.

problem: Readwise Reader's mobile app is described as somewhat laggy with large libraries; reviewers say desktop/web is the stronger experience.

sources.title: Asian Efficiency: Readwise Reader review

saga_solution: Local database with incremental indexing so library size does not affect scroll performance on phone or Leaf.

problem: MobileRead users still say no e-ink reader matches a tablet for PDFs; large Boox devices or column-splitting/reflow are the compromises. Small-screen e-readers handle academic PDFs poorly.

sources.title: MobileRead: Best e-reader for PDFs in 2025
The eBook Reader: PDF showdown ranking readers

workarounds: KOReader reflow (k2pdfopt); large tablets; crop margins.
saga_solution: PDF mode with auto-crop margins, column detection, text reflow for text-layer PDFs; route PDFs to phone/desktop and send only reflowed text to the Leaf.

problem: KOReader is loved for PDF handling far beyond stock firmware (reflow, cropping, contrast and font thickening).

sources.title: LWN: KOReader article and comments
TechTactician: PocketBook with KOReader

saga_solution: Benchmark SAGA's PDF tools against KOReader's crop/reflow on the same test PDFs before launch.

problem: KOReader's deep customization (programmable gestures, style tweaks, frontlight shortcuts) is the main reason power users install it.

sources.title: LWN: KOReader
ZSA Loves: KOReader

saga_solution: Offer gesture/tap-zone mapping and saved reading profiles, but behind an 'Advanced' layer.

problem: KOReader's settings are described as labyrinthine; one user needed hundreds of adjustments to get comfortable. Power comes at the cost of approachability.

sources.title: LWN: KOReader comments
Tildes: KOReader discussion

workarounds: Copy someone else's settings file; follow guides.
saga_solution: Progressive disclosure: 5 essential settings on the reading screen, full control in Advanced; ship presets ('Classic', 'Large print', 'Dyslexia-friendly', 'Compact Leaf').

problem: Kindle e-readers show lockscreen ads ('Special Offers') unless the buyer pays extra to remove them; reviewers note Kobo shows none, and lockscreens have even promoted low-quality AI-generated books.

sources.title: BGR: How to turn off ads on your Kindle
Laptop Mag: Kindle vs Kobo
Yahoo: Kindle lock screens showing ads for AI-generated books

workarounds: Pay to remove ads; ask support to remove.
saga_solution: No ads or store promotions anywhere in the reading UI or Leaf sleep screen; sleep screen shows the current book cover or user image.

problem: Readwise Reader costs around $10/month (more billed monthly), which reviewers call steep for a reading app when free options exist, and its value takes weeks to appear.

sources.title: Asian Efficiency: Readwise Reader review
Activepieces: Readwise pricing 2026 guide

workarounds: Annual billing; Lite tier; free alternatives.
saga_solution: Core reading, import, local stats and export free forever; charge only for optional hosted sync/storage and the Leaf hardware.

problem: BookFusion users note that uploading large libraries requires a paid subscription, adding cost for people already leaving Kindle/Audible.

sources.title: Tildes: BookFusion discussion

saga_solution: Local library has no size limit; paid sync tiers priced on storage with a generous free tier for metadata/annotation sync (small) separate from file sync (large).

problem: Readwise Reader is valued for pushing highlights automatically into Notion/Obsidian, importing Kindle highlights, and resurfacing highlights via spaced repetition.

sources.title: Asian Efficiency: Readwise Reader review
Readwise Reader update Dec 2025

saga_solution: Export highlights as Markdown/JSON automatically to a chosen folder (works with Obsidian vaults) and offer a Readwise export target.

problem: BookFusion's Calibre plugin and cross-device library are liked by users with DRM-free collections, who say those files stop being second-class citizens.

sources.title: Tildes: BookFusion discussion
BookFusion docs: Calibre plugin
BookFusion feature board: sync Calibre highlights

saga_solution: Calibre import that preserves metadata, tags, series and custom columns; optional Calibre content-server/OPDS connection.

problem: Kindle's store size, frequent deals and Kindle Unlimited are among the main reasons people stay, along with cheap, reliable hardware and Prime delivery.

sources.title: SlashGear: 3 things Kindle owners love most
Laptop Mag: Kindle vs Kobo (Kindle still wins on accessories/delivery)
The eBook Reader: Kindle + Kobo is the best combination

saga_solution: Don't compete with the store; make SAGA the best home for books bought elsewhere (DRM-free stores, Humble/StoryBundle, Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks) with built-in OPDS catalog browsing.

problem: Goodreads (Amazon-owned) is criticised as stagnant: dated design, buggy apps, few new features; many users moved to StoryGraph partly to avoid Amazon.

sources.title: MakeUseOf: 6 reasons to stop using Goodreads
HuffPost: people leaving Goodreads for StoryGraph

saga_solution: Optional export of finished books/ratings to StoryGraph/Goodreads CSV formats; never require a social account.

problem: Kobo's built-in OverDrive lets readers borrow library ebooks directly on the device, a major reason readers outside the US (where Kindle Libby delivery is unavailable) pick Kobo.

sources.title: SlashGear: Is Libby compatible with Kobo?
Libby Help: reading Libby ebooks on a Kobo
NBC Select: Kobo Libra Colour review

saga_solution: Library lending requires DRM licensing SAGA won't have at launch; instead deep-link to Libby and support Adobe/LCP-free library EPUBs where offered (e.g., public domain). Be honest in marketing that SAGA is for DRM-free books.

problem: Libby users in the US report some new releases cannot be sent to Kindle immediately (or ever) because of publisher/Amazon authorization, forcing reading in the Libby app.

sources.title: Boing Boing: new Libby ebooks not available on Kindle, wait a day

workarounds: Read in Libby app; wait 1-2 days.
saga_solution: n/a for DRM content; note as a reason Libby users may still need Libby alongside SAGA.

problem: Kindle e-reader TTS is only available through VoiceView, an accessibility screen reader buried in settings, needing Bluetooth audio, ~18 gestures, and English only; Fire tablets have a much easier TTS.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: why is TTS so difficult on Kindles
TeleRead: I'm blind - Kindle TTS has been a nightmare

workarounds: Use Kindle app on phone with system TTS; Fire tablet.
saga_solution: First-class 'Listen' button in reading UI using OS voices (and optional on-device neural voices), sentence highlighting, sleep timer, continues with screen off.

problem: Kobo e-readers lack general text-to-speech for ebooks (commenters note it), while PocketBook's official TTS is a reason some prefer PocketBook.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: Kindle TTS article (comment on Kobo)
TechTactician: PocketBook official TTS

saga_solution: TTS in the phone app that can follow along on the Leaf (page turns in sync).

problem: BookFusion's listening controls (skip by sentence) and EPUB 3 Media Overlay read-along support are singled out as better than Kindle's.

sources.title: Tildes: BookFusion discussion

saga_solution: Support EPUB 3 Media Overlays (pre-recorded narration synced to text) and sentence-level skip in TTS.

problem: The US National Federation of the Blind has long documented gaps in Amazon device accessibility; blind users describe Kindle e-reader accessibility as hard to learn.

sources.title: NFB: The state of Amazon device accessibility
TeleRead: Kindle TTS a nightmare for blind user

saga_solution: Build with platform accessibility APIs from day one: VoiceOver/TalkBack labels, logical focus order, reading-content exposure to screen readers, test with blind users before launch.

problem: Thorium Reader is recognised by the DAISY Consortium for accessibility work (screen-reader support, EPUB 3 accessibility, read-aloud), showing what a reader built for accessibility looks like.

sources.title: DAISY: Thorium 1.8.0 accessibility improvements
Thorium docs: accessibility

saga_solution: Use Thorium/Readium accessibility behaviour as SAGA's accessibility test baseline.

problem: Dyslexia-friendly fonts are frequently requested, but literacy research suggests spacing and layout matter more than special typefaces; readers need control of letter, word and line spacing, not just one font.

sources.title: Shanahan on Literacy: special fonts for dyslexia
Popular Science: ebook readers make reading easier for people with dyslexia

saga_solution: Bundle OpenDyslexic/Atkinson Hyperlegible plus letter/word/line spacing, short-line mode and optional line focus ruler; avoid overclaiming that a font 'fixes' dyslexia.

problem: Amazon dropped MOBI from Send-to-Kindle and converts EPUBs on its side; some files fail conversion or lose formatting, and users depend on Amazon's pipeline to read their own files.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: Amazon dropping MOBI on Send-to-Kindle
MobileRead: Send-to-Kindle EPUB thread

workarounds: Convert with Calibre first; fix EPUB errors.
saga_solution: Read EPUB natively without server conversion; validate on import and repair common EPUB errors locally with a report.

problem: Google Play Books uploads sometimes fail with EPUB processing errors, and users hit opaque failures with files that open fine elsewhere.

sources.title: OSTechNix: fix EPUB processing error in Google Play Books
Adobe Community: Google Play Books upload error

saga_solution: Local import never depends on a server; when a file is malformed, open it anyway in a tolerant mode and explain what's wrong.

problem: The Xteink X4 community (CrossPoint) supports Calibre wireless send and browser upload, which reviewers say turns a limited gadget into a joy.

sources.title: Aftermath: Xteink X4 / CrossPoint review

saga_solution: Leaf supports Calibre wireless device protocol and OPDS pull in addition to the SAGA app.

problem: Calibre remains the power tool for managing ebook libraries (metadata, conversion, device management) despite a long-criticised interface.

sources.title: LWN: Calibrating Calibre 1.0
OMG! Ubuntu: Calibre 4.0 released

saga_solution: Import Calibre libraries losslessly; don't try to replace Calibre for power users — interoperate.

problem: Calibre's interface is widely called dated and cluttered; newcomers find it intimidating even though it is powerful.

sources.title: Slashdot: Calibre 1.0 released (comments)
OMG! Ubuntu: making Calibre look nicer
MobileRead: Calibre UI discussion

saga_solution: Simple library: shelves, tags, series, auto-metadata from the file, smart collections; bulk edit for power users.

problem: Kindle limits how much of a publisher's book you can export as highlights (clipping limit), truncating notes, and highlights on personal documents need workarounds to export.

sources.title: Readwise docs: Kindle highlights import / truncation
Instructables: export Kindle highlights incl. personal documents
Hongkiat: export Kindle notes and highlights

workarounds: My Clippings.txt from device; third-party exporters.
saga_solution: No export limits on your own files; export highlights with chapter, location, colour, note and timestamp as Markdown, JSON, CSV, and annotated EPUB.

problem: Apple Books users report books corrupting and PDF highlights being wiped, and EPUBs disappearing after iOS updates, with no way to recover annotations.

sources.title: Apple Community: Apple Books corrupted my book and wiped all my PDF highlights
Apple Community: EPUB books disappeared after iOS 15.4

workarounds: Back up via Mac; export notes regularly.
saga_solution: Annotations stored separately from the book file with versioned history and automatic local backups; restoring a book never deletes its notes.

problem: Google Play Books can save notes and highlights to a Google Drive document, which users like for studying.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: Google Play Books now syncs notes to Google Drive

saga_solution: Auto-export annotations to a user-chosen folder (local, iCloud Drive, Google Drive) as a live Markdown file per book.

problem: StoryGraph is liked for detailed reading stats and mood/pace charts, plus features Goodreads lacked such as DNF and partial-star ratings.

sources.title: Book Riot: StoryGraph review
MakeUseOf: reasons to stop using Goodreads (no DNF, whole stars)
NewsBytes: Goodreads finally gets half and quarter star ratings

saga_solution: On-device stats (time read, pages/day, streaks, finish estimates, genre breakdowns) with DNF state, no social obligation, CSV export.

problem: Amazon restored an 'Assistive Reader' read-aloud mode on recent Kindles in Aug 2025 after previously pulling it, but it needs Bluetooth audio, is not officially announced, and a commenter reports it works only on Amazon-purchased books, not sideloads.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: Kindle software update brings back TTS

workarounds: Use phone app TTS; Fire tablet.
saga_solution: TTS treats every file equally, works on phone speaker without pairing, and is never remotely withdrawn.

problem: Amazon officially offers OpenDyslexic on Kindle (since 2016) together with larger sizes and spacing/margin controls, which accessibility advocates count as a baseline others should match.

sources.title: About Amazon: new accessibility features for Kindle e-readers
Kobo Help: fonts on Kobo eReader

saga_solution: Ship OpenDyslexic and Atkinson Hyperlegible by default on app and Leaf.

problem: Moon+ Reader syncs positions, highlights and bookmarks through the user's own Dropbox or WebDAV rather than a vendor cloud, which suits privacy-minded Android users.

sources.title: Moon+ Reader FAQ

saga_solution: Offer 'bring your own storage' sync backends (WebDAV, iCloud Drive, Dropbox, Syncthing folder) alongside SAGA's hosted sync.

problem: Kindle owners list navigation friction: footnote pop-ups show only the first paragraph, there is no back button from search results, tap zones can't be customised, and menus take several taps.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: What are some things you don't like about Kindles?

workarounds: Use Page Flip; tap back via 'Go to'.
saga_solution: Full-length footnote pop-ups with 'open in place', a persistent back stack (search, links, footnotes all reversible), and remappable tap zones.

problem: Accidental page turns are a recurring Kindle gripe: bezel touches and swipes flip pages or change font size, and newer models dropped physical page-turn buttons, with touch not always disable-able.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: What are some things you don't like about Kindles?

workarounds: Lock screen orientation; buy Kobo/PocketBook with buttons.
saga_solution: SAGA Leaf uses physical buttons as the primary input; phone app offers a 'touch lock' and lets users disable pinch-to-zoom font changes.

problem: In the Kindle app, reading position sometimes jumps back tens of pages after syncing, according to summaries of low-star app store reviews.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)

saga_solution: Never move the reader backward silently; when a remote position differs, show a non-blocking 'Jump to p. X from Leaf?' prompt.

problem: Kindles have been reported to wipe Calibre-sideloaded books after long periods in airplane mode followed by reconnection; Amazon never confirmed a cause and updates through 2024 did not fix it. This hits exactly the readers who go offline on purpose.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: Kindle ereaders deleting sideloaded ebooks
The eBook Reader: Beware of airplane mode on Kindles if you sideload

workarounds: Keep Wi-Fi always on or always off; keep backups.
saga_solution: Local files are never removed by sync; deletes require explicit user action and go to a recoverable 'Recently deleted' for 30 days, on app and Leaf.

problem: A traveller's Kindle could not get past a hotel Wi-Fi login page and queued library books had never actually downloaded, so the books were unavailable until they found open Wi-Fi.

sources.title: TechRadar: A vacation Amazon Kindle near-disaster

workarounds: Download everything before travel; phone hotspot.
saga_solution: Make download state obvious (fully on device vs. cloud-only), offer 'keep next N books on device', and let the Leaf receive books over phone-to-device Bluetooth/Wi-Fi Direct without any internet.

problem: Cloud-first readers need pre-caching to work offline: Readwise Reader asks users to open the app first and choose offline sections, and Readest users requested an offline mode for its web/PWA version.

sources.title: Readwise Reader FAQs (offline)
Readest issues list (#247 offline mode for PWA)

workarounds: Open app before going offline; use native app.
saga_solution: Local-first architecture: the library lives on-device and the cloud is a replica, so offline is the default state, not a mode.

problem: Libby audiobooks are large and sometimes fail to play offline, and loans expire after 14-21 days, according to summaries of negative app reviews.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)

workarounds: Download over Wi-Fi in advance; renew early.
saga_solution: For SAGA's own files: no expiry, no licence checks, and storage usage visible per book.

problem: A 2024 Kindle firmware update brought user reports of lag, freezes, battery drain while idle, fonts reverting to Bookerly, and a tiny progress indicator; not every device was affected and Amazon didn't confirm.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: More problems caused by latest Kindle software update

saga_solution: Staged rollouts for Leaf firmware with a one-tap rollback, and preference migrations tested so updates never reset fonts or layout.

problem: Weeks-long battery life is one of the three things Kindle owners praise most.

sources.title: SlashGear: 3 things Kindle owners say they love most

saga_solution: Leaf target: 2+ weeks at 1 hr/day with front light; deep sleep between page turns; phone app must not drain battery with background sync.

problem: KOReader users build self-hosted dashboards (KoInsight, KoShelf) to see their reading statistics and notes outside the device, showing demand for owned, exportable reading stats.

sources.title: Bright Coding: KoInsight self-hosted dashboard for KOReader stats
Bright Coding: KoShelf reading dashboard
KoInsight on GitHub

saga_solution: Built-in stats dashboard merging sessions from phone, desktop and Leaf, stored locally, exportable as CSV/SQLite.

problem: Community KOReader plugins add cover-based home screens with progress and reading streaks, implying the stock experience lacks motivating habit features.

sources.title: Boredom at Work: 10 best KOReader plugins (SimpleUI streaks)

saga_solution: Optional, gentle streaks and goals (off by default, no guilt notifications); Leaf sleep screen can show progress.

problem: Syncing position between a tiny ESP32 reader (Xteink X4 on CrossPoint) and KOReader is hard: memory limits prevent full-book layout, positions drifted 2-3 pages, and large books crashed during indexing.

sources.title: CrossPoint GitHub discussion #61: KOReader progress sync

saga_solution: Have the phone app pre-paginate/pre-process books for the Leaf (chapter-split, pre-indexed anchors) so position maps by stable text anchors (CFI-like), not page numbers.

problem: Kindle libraries can't sort or filter by series or author well, collections are hard to manage for Calibre users, and sort settings don't carry into collections.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: What are some things you don't like about Kindles?

saga_solution: Series-aware library (read from EPUB/Calibre metadata), sort/filter by author, series, tag, status, with saved views shared across devices.

problem: Readest users requested recursive import of a folder of books, a basic need for people moving existing libraries.

sources.title: Readest issues list (#179 import directory recursively)

saga_solution: Watch-folder and recursive import with dedupe by content hash.

problem: Readest users asked to self-host its web reader and sync API rather than depend on the developer's cloud.

sources.title: Readest issues list (#192 self-hosting sync)

saga_solution: Documented, open sync protocol with a self-hostable server option; also folder-based sync via iCloud Drive/Syncthing.

problem: Custom font support is a recurring request for newer readers (open Readest feature request) and Kindle commenters complain fonts apply globally, not per book.

sources.title: Readest issues list (#237 custom fonts)
The eBook Reader: What are some things you don't like about Kindles?

saga_solution: Drag-in TTF/OTF fonts that sync (where licence allows) to every device and convert to Leaf bitmap format; per-book overrides.

problem: Kindle typography controls are limited compared with Kobo: few usable font sizes, only three margin and line-spacing settings.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: What are some things you don't like about Kindles?

saga_solution: Continuous sliders (with sensible steps) for size, margins, line height, paragraph spacing.

problem: Moon+ Reader's free version shows a home-screen banner and occasional full-screen ads, and PDF support needs the paid Pro upgrade.

sources.title: Yahoo Tech: Moon+ Reader review

saga_solution: No ads, ever; PDF and EPUB both free.

problem: Moon+ Reader is praised as a smooth, highly customisable Android reader: many themes with auto day/night switching, gesture/tap mapping, TTS and dictionaries.

sources.title: Yahoo Tech: Moon+ Reader review
MobileRead Wiki: Moon+ Reader

saga_solution: Match Moon+ on themes and auto day/night; keep the UI cleaner than Moon+.

problem: Kobo Plus titles rotate out and it isn't always clear which books are included, per summaries of negative reviews.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)

saga_solution: No rotating catalogue; anything imported stays.

problem: Popular Libby bestsellers can take 8-16 weeks of waiting, and libraries are tightening hold rules (e.g., suspended holds now auto-cancel after a year) to speed circulation.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)
TRL: Libby holds are changing

workarounds: Multiple library cards; buy the book.
saga_solution: Out of scope for DRM loans; SAGA can show 'available free' links for public-domain editions (Standard Ebooks/Gutenberg).

problem: Libby is loved for being free, supporting local libraries, and having no ads or recommendation clutter.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)
Everyday Reading: Why I love the Libby app

saga_solution: Adopt Libby's calm, clutter-free tone; never put store promotion on the home screen.

problem: Kindle's app home screen is dominated by recommendations, and Kindle devices push the store heavily.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)
The eBook Reader: What are some things you don't like about Kindles?

saga_solution: Home opens to 'Continue reading' and your shelves; no store.

problem: Apple Books annotation export is per-book and awkward for heavy note-takers.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)

workarounds: Email notes per book; third-party exporters.
saga_solution: Library-wide annotation view with search and bulk export.

problem: Apple Books handles sideloaded EPUBs and PDFs smoothly with no extra account, and is preinstalled with a clean UI.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)

saga_solution: Match the 'open in' import ease on iOS: share sheet, Files app, AirDrop.

problem: Getting non-Kobo EPUBs into the Kobo iOS app requires a desktop workflow, per review summaries.

sources.title: Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)

saga_solution: Import directly on phone from Files, share sheet, browser downloads, OPDS.

problem: PocketBook devices are praised for broad format support (EPUB, PDF, MOBI, FB2, comics, DRM-free AZW), multilingual TTS, and free cloud storage for moving books between devices.

sources.title: Notebookcheck: PocketBook Verse Pro Color review
Expert Reviews: PocketBook InkPad One - diverse file support

saga_solution: Support EPUB, PDF, TXT, and add FB2/CBZ/DRM-free AZW3 import (convert to EPUB) early.

problem: Whispersync's link between Kindle text and Audible narration lets readers swap between reading and listening without losing their place; Apple Books doesn't link audio and ebook positions automatically.

sources.title: Android Authority: the Kindle feature stopping me switching
Unstar: Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo, Libby, Scribd apps ranked 2026 (summary of 1-3 star reviews)

saga_solution: TTS-based 'listen from here' that hands off exactly to reading position; later, align user-owned DRM-free audiobooks to EPUB text (forced alignment).

problem: Readest users request custom TTS engines, and its free AI voices are time-capped with paid plans for more.

sources.title: Readest issues list (#258 custom TTS engine)
Make Tech Easier: Readest ebook reader

saga_solution: Default to free on-device/OS voices; pluggable engines.

problem: Readest's side-by-side parallel reading of two books is singled out as useful for language learning and research, alongside built-in dictionary and Wikipedia lookups.

sources.title: Make Tech Easier: Readest ebook reader

saga_solution: Desktop split view (book + book, or book + notes) and offline dictionary packs.

problem: Readest sync can take minutes, a book can't be removed from its cloud directly, and syncing requires an account.

sources.title: Make Tech Easier: Readest ebook reader

workarounds: Delete from originating device and re-upload.
saga_solution: Near-real-time position sync (small payloads), clear per-book 'remove from cloud / remove from device' controls.

problem: Kobo's seamless Calibre support and the ability to install KOReader without jailbreaking are cited as reasons tinkerers prefer Kobo; Kindle's advantage is syncing Send-to-Kindle docs.

sources.title: The eBook Reader: Kindle + Kobo is the best combination

saga_solution: Leaf should be open: documented transfer protocol, Calibre device driver, user-flashable firmware.
